For clarity, the Regulatory Innovation Bloc’s non‑negotiables are: an open, machine‑readable core schema (JSON‑LD or equivalent) with a narrowly defined set of mandatory minimal fields; explicit mapping rules to existing systems to eliminate duplicate entry; built‑in privacy/security and role‑based access controls; and a time‑limited central‑agency pilot subject to independent, cost‑neutral evaluation with an automatic review/sunset checkpoint before any wider mandate — plus an explicit prohibition on authorizing new permanent funding or staffing via this bill.  

We are prepared to be flexible on the exact serialization (JSON‑LD preferred but equivalent formats acceptable), the number/location of optional metadata beyond the mandatory minimum, and minor adjustments to pilot duration (±3 months) or initial agency scope so long as the pilot and prohibitions above remain intact.  

We will not accept language that permits departments to reclassify pilot costs as baseline staffing or recurring budget items; the operative text must require transparent reporting of resource use and bar budget reclassification.  

If Fiscal and the other blocs accept those boundaries, Regulatory Innovation will immediately join a joint technical working group to finalize the core schema and operative clauses within one week for submission at markup.  

If you need firmer draft language for the prohibition/reporting clause before committing, tell us the precise standards you require and we will circulate legally drafted text within 48 hours.
